blocks.vo_line: August 28th. The Moon turns to shadow. One night. Don't miss it.
This is the Corn Moon. The final one before autumn. And this year, it doesn't just rise.
It gets partially eaten. Earth slides between the Sun and the Moon.
A dark bite grows across the surface. Right in front of you. No telescope. Nothing to set up. Just look up.
Two weeks ago, the Sun went dark behind the Moon. This time, Earth returns the favor.
It peaks after moonrise. Visible across the Americas, Europe, and Africa. Then it's gone.
So here's my question. When it happens, are you outside? Or are you scrolling, and seeing the photos tomorrow, wishing you'd looked?
Tell me below. I'm reading every single one.
